synopsis: 4593a4aa (Oak debrief) and 97434e3d (Pine debrief) both ended as HTTP 200 unavailable/provider_rate_limit with the Groq-vocabulary diagnostic rate_limit_exceeded and a 21 s retry hint. This is consistent with the expected sequence (Gemini limited, then Groq per-minute token rejection reclassified as a rate limit). The bundle contains no per-provider attempt record, so the Gemini step is inferred, not observed. 8a6b7e0f (Lake debrief) ended HTTP 503 codex_unavailable. In features.ts, any output that still fails host validation after the single repair throws CodexFailure('unavailable') regardless of which provider generated it, and http.ts renders that as codex_<kind>. A Gemini- or Groq-served debrief that failed validation twice is therefore reported as Codex unavailable. The suspected misattribution is confirmed at source level, with the failing stage at feature validation and repair. The specific validator cannot be identified because the provider's output and the validation reason are not in the bundle. fa67ddf4 (director): the second provider generation issued two host tool calls (inspectScene, evaluateResources), both returning the unchanged minute-0 state, then the gateway returned provider_or_validation_failure. 4499ec96 (Groq director, generation 2) issued one preview of requestDecision, then the same generic failure. The bundles do not show the misdescribed_gap_check rejection or the groq_rate_limit outcome reported by the work order; those reside only in gateway metrics, outside this capture.
